diagnostics.message: :resource.null_resource.wait_for_cluster: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_eks_cluster.this is redundant — already implied by attribute references

`null_resource.wait_for_cluster` lists `aws_eks_cluster.this` in its `depends_on`, but it already references `aws_eks_cluster.this[0].endpoint` in its `environment` block, which establishes the same ordering implicitly. The `depends_on` entry for the cluster duplicates the existing attribute reference (the `aws_security_group_rule.cluster_private_access` entry is still needed).

`aws_eks_node_group.workers` already references `random_pet.node_groups[each.key]` (in the `node_group_name` default), and that `random_pet` resource itself carries `depends_on = [var.ng_depends_on]`. The node group therefore already waits for every resource in `ng_depends_on` (EKS cluster, aws-auth ConfigMap, worker policy attachments) transitively, so repeating `depends_on = [var.ng_depends_on]` on the node group duplicates an ordering edge that already exists.

`aws_eks_cluster.this` only waits on the two managed policy attachments and the log group, not on `aws_iam_role_policy.cluster_elb_sl_role_creation`, which grants the cluster role the EC2 permissions EKS needs to create `AWSServiceRoleForElasticLoadBalancing` during load balancer provisioning. Nothing in the cluster resource references that inline role policy, so cluster provisioning can start (and later load balancer provisioning can fail) before the policy exists. The AWS provider documentation for `aws_eks_cluster.role_arn` explicitly requires an explicit dependency on IAM role policy/policy-attachment resources. Add it to the cluster's `depends_on`.

`aws_autoscaling_group.workers` instances boot and immediately try to register with the cluster, authenticating with the worker IAM role, which must already be mapped in the `aws-auth` ConfigMap (`kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth`). The ASG only depends on the cluster, launch configuration and `random_pet.workers`, so instances can launch before the ConfigMap maps their role and fail to join the cluster. This operational ordering is not expressed anywhere; it needs an explicit `depends_on = [kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth]`.

Same issue as the Launch Configuration worker group: `aws_autoscaling_group.workers_launch_template` only depends on the cluster, the launch template and `random_pet.workers_launch_template`. Instances it launches authenticate with the worker IAM role, which must already be present in the `aws-auth` ConfigMap (`kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth`) before the nodes can join; nothing expresses that ordering, so add `depends_on = [kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth]`.
